record_type_quote: In the present contribution, we present a replication of the race-erased effect reported by Kurzban et al.

targets.authors: Kurzban R., Tooby J., Cosmides L.
targets.title: Can race be erased? Coalitional computation and social categorization.
targets.evidence_quote: In light of the ongoing discussion between advocates of automatic encoding of race and researchers claiming that no special role is played by race, the key findings by Kurzban et al. (2001) that form the object of our replication proposal are that race encoding can be decreased in coalitional contexts, and that arbitrary cues other than racial appearance can play a role similar to that of race in earlier claims of automatic race encoding.
targets.outcome_quote: Our replication qualitatively supports the results reported by Kurzban et al. (2001).
targets.outcome_reasoning: The authors explicitly give an overall qualitative-support verdict, and both preregistered hypotheses meet their stated replication criterion. Smaller effects and lack of total erasure qualify the magnitude without overriding that overall verdict.

reasoning: Full text identity verified against title, DOI, Wouter Voorspoels, Annelies Bartlema and Wolf Vanpaemel. Completed preregistered new-sample study re-tests Kurzban et al. (2001). The two conditions correspond to original Experiments 1 and 2 and their within-paper replication in 5 and 6, all one target publication. Johnson and Cesario (2013) provides materials and power-analysis information, not a separately re-tested target.
